chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Al-Husayn ibn Saeed, from his brother Al-Hasan, from Zurara, from Sama'ah, who said:

I asked him (peace be upon him) about the slave whose master contracts him (for manumission), and he knows that he does not possess little or much. He (peace be upon him) said: 'He should contract him, and if he asks the people, he is not prevented from contracting him on account of not having wealth, for Allah provides for the servants, some from others, and the Believer is assisted, and it is said, and the Benevolent is assisted.'
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling if a slave has no money but wants to contract for freedom?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi clarifies that a master cannot withhold mukatabah (contracted manumission) simply due to the slave's current lack of funds, emphasizing that divine sustenance (rizq) circulates among people. It highlights the theological principle that believers and the righteous are actively supported by God, encouraging masters to facilitate emancipation as an act of faith rather than a financial transaction. This ruling underscores the Shia emphasis on removing barriers to freedom and recognizing God's role in providing means for those striving for liberation.

en.hubeali: A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Isa, from Al Husayn Bin Saeed, from his brother Al Hassan, from Zurara, from Sama’at who said,

‘I asked him<sup>asws</sup> about the slave whose master contracted him, and he knew that he would not own little or more. He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘He should contract him, and if the people had asked, he would not be prevented from contracting him from a term if there is not wealth for him, for Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Sustains the servants, from each other, and the Believer is Assisted, and it is said, ‘And the benevolent is Assisted’’.
